agenda: Set a blameless frame and reconstruct Tuesday's 52-minute optimizer outage.
Trace the database index change, nightly table lock, and delayed detection.
Account for the 31 affected customers and review communication and recovery.
Agree owners and dates for alert thresholds, deploy checks, and status-page updates.

chapters.title: Incident Timeline and Recovery
beats: Mei establishes a blameless review of Tuesday's 52-minute incident; Lucas reconstructs the index deploy and the nightly job's table lock.
The optimizer returned empty route results rather than its last good plan, and dispatchers first reported missing routes before the alert paged engineering.
The team stopped the job, rolled back the index change, and checked route regeneration before declaring recovery.

chapters.title: Root Cause and Detection Gap
beats: Lucas explains how the changed index caused the nightly job to take a locking query path; the job and optimizer contended for the same tables.
Mei and Lucas disagree about whether an alert on empty route results or database lock duration should be the primary page; they agree to pair a customer-visible route signal with a lock diagnostic.
Jonas challenges the empty-state design because it looked like a successful zero-route result rather than an error.

chapters.title: Customer Impact and Communication
beats: Amara verifies 31 affected customers and distinguishes failed route requests from customers who merely opened the board during the window.
Amara and Omar challenge the delayed status-page post and the lack of a dependable notification owner.
The group agrees on evidence-based customer follow-up without implying that all 31 customers lost deliveries.

chapters.title: Prevention, Owners, and Close
beats: Mei commits to a deploy checklist that checks index and nightly-job interaction and requires an explicit rollback owner.
Lucas commits to alert thresholds and a replay test; Jonas owns an explicit route-error state, while Amara owns customer and status-page wording.
Omar requests measurable completion evidence and a short review, and Mei closes with owners and deadlines.
